Based on my search, I can provide you with a comprehensive explanation of what globalization means.

## What Is Globalization?

**Globalization** refers to the increasing connectedness, interdependence, and integration of countries, cultures, and economies around the world. It describes how trade, technology, information, and people move more freely across national borders, making the world more interconnected than ever before.

### Core Definition

According to the Cambridge Dictionary, globalization is "the increase of trade around the world, especially by large companies producing and trading goods in many different countries." However, most scholars and institutions recognize that globalization extends far beyond just trade.

The International Monetary Fund offers a more comprehensive definition: globalization refers to "the increasing integration of economies worldwide, particularly through the movement of goods, services, and capital across borders," and sometimes also includes the movement of people (labor) and knowledge (technology) across international borders, along with broader cultural, political, and environmental dimensions.

### Key Dimensions of Globalization

Globalization operates across multiple interconnected dimensions:

| Dimension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Economic Globalization** | Integration of national economies through international trade, foreign investment, and the rise of multinational corporations |
| **Cultural Globalization** | Spread of ideas, information, cultural practices, and media across borders (e.g., Hollywood movies shown worldwide) |
| **Political Globalization** | Growing importance of international organizations (UN, EU, WTO) and increasing cooperation between governments |
| **Technological Globalization** | Worldwide interconnection through digital communication, social media, and the internet |
| **Financial Globalization** | Increased ease of money flow between countries for business, investment, and personal transactions |

### Historical Context

Globalization is not entirely new. Early examples include:
- **The Silk Road** (50 B.C.E. – 250 C.E.): An ancient network of trade routes connecting China, Central Asia, and the Mediterranean
- **The Age of Exploration** (15th–17th centuries): European explorers established sea routes connecting previously unconnected continents
- **The Industrial Revolution**: Created foundational infrastructure for further economic integration

What makes **modern globalization unique** is its unprecedented scale, speed, and complexity—driven by advances in transportation, communication technologies, and digital networks.

### The "Global Village" Concept

A helpful way to understand globalization is the "global village" analogy: imagine the world as a village where actions in one corner rapidly influence every other part. For example, buying a cup of coffee in New York may involve beans grown in Brazil, roasted in Italy, with the transaction processed through global financial systems.

### Why It Matters

According to the World Bank, international trade accounts for more than 50% of global GDP, demonstrating how deeply interconnected national economies have become. Even local actions can now ripple across continents due to interconnected supply chains, financial markets, and communication networks.

In essence, globalization represents both a **process** (of increasing integration) and a **condition** (of being interconnected), shaping nearly every aspect of contemporary life—from the products we buy and the food we eat to the ideas we encounter and the jobs available to us.

Sources:
1. https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/globalization
2. https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/globalization/
3. https://www.vistatec.com/globilization-concept-cause-and-consequences/
4. https://www.mywestford.com/blog/what-is-gobalization-in-todays-world/
5. https://esg.sustainability-directory.com/term/globalization-impact/
6. https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/globalization-meaning-and-essence
7. https://facts.net/society-and-social-sciences/20-facts-about-the-effects-of-globalization/
